questions.question: As a reaction to Rowlatt Act, _________ was organised as National Humiliation Day.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **6th April 1919 was organised as National Humiliation day as a reaction to Rowlatt Act**__.
 
• Rowlatt Act was officially known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Act,1919.
 
• It was passed in March 1919 by the Imperial Legislative Council.
 
• The Act gave the authority to the Britishers to detain anybody suspected of terrorist activities without any trials.

questions.question: In 2018, Amnesty International stripped _________ of the Ambassador of Conscience Award given in 2009.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Amnesty International stripped Aung San Suu Kyi of the Ambassador of Conscience Award given in 2009**__.
 
• Amnesty International is a British Non-Governmental Organisation and its work is focused on the protection of Human Rights.
 
• The move came from the NGO in November 2018 after the failure of Aung San Suu Kyi and her government to speak out about military atrocities against the Rohingya Population in Myanmar.

questions.question: In economic terms what do we mean by 'intermediate goods'?

options.text: Goods sold between industries for the resale or production of other goods
Goods in transit before reaching the consumers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e. __Intermediate goods__ ​

 
• **Intermediate goods **are the goods sold between industries for the resale or production of other goods.
 
• These products are also called semi-finished products because they are used as inputs to become part of the finished products.
 
• Examples of intermediate goods are Salt, Sugar, etc.

questions.question: In which year was the term 'Gross Happiness Index' coined by the fourth king of Bhutan, Jigme Singye Wangchuck?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The term "**Gross Happiness Index**__" was coined by **__Jigme Singye Wangchuk in 1972__**.
 
• This index is still used by the government of Bhutan to measure the collective happiness and the well-being of a population of Bhutan.
 
• The first Prime Minister of Bhutan was __**Jigme Palden Doorji**__.

questions.question: The Khilafat Movement of 1920 was organised as a protest against the injustice done to _______.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Khilafat Movement__ was organised as a protest against the injustice done to __**Turkey**__.
 
• It was organised by the Indian Muslims in 1919 to recover the Caliph of Turkey as a symbol of unity among Muslim community in India.
 
• The movement was also supported by Mahatma Gandhi's Non-Cooperation movement.
 
• It was launched by brothers __**Shaukat and Muhammad Ali**__ and by __**Abdul Kalam Azad**__.
 
• The movement collapsed in 1924.

questions.question: What is the term used to describe the angular distance of a place north or south of Earth's equator?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Latitude__** is defined as the angular distance of a place north or south of Earth's equator.
 
• __**Pole**__ is a point on the either side of the surface of the Earth where lines of longitude meet.
 
• The Earth is divided by the 0 degree latitude into equal halves known as __**Hemisphere**__.
 
• **__Longitude__** are defined as the imaginary lines that bisects the globe through the North and South poles.

questions.question: Which of the following is the third stage in the metamorphosis of a butterﬂy?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **There are four stages in the process of Metamorphosis of a butterfly**__.
 
• The first stage is the egg.
 
• The Butterfly eggs are laid on the plants by the female Butterfly.
 
• The second stage is the larva stage in which the butterfly exists in the form of a caterpillar.
 
• The Third stage is Pupa which is transitional phase in which the Caterpillar changes into Butterfly.
 
• The fourth stage is the Adult stage in which a full grown adult butterfly comes out of the pupa.

questions.question: A traditional 'battery' contains which of the following chemicals?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **The Traditional battery contains Sulfuric acid**__.
 
• The Battery acid is 30-50% sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) in water.
 
• The Sulfuric acid is used as an electrolyte.
 
• The Traditional battery consists of two metals plates separated by a liquid or gel containing sulfuric acid in water.
 
• When the battery is in the use, the electrons move from the negatively-charged plate to the positively-charged plate.

questions.question: How many 'canine teeth' does an adult human have?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Human beings**__ have four types of teeth which are **__Incisors, Canine, Molar and __**__Premolar__.
 
• A normal adult mouth has 32 teeth.
 
• Incisors (8) help in biting into the food.
 
• Canines (4) help in tearing the food.
 
• Molars (12) help in grinding the food.
 
• Premolars (8) help in crushing the food.

questions.question: What is the deﬁnition for the term 'hibernation'?

options.text: A habit of food conservation during summer season for winter among animals
Building of habitat (nests) by birds to save themselves in rainy season
A state of reduced metabolic activity during winter season among some animals
A state of hyperactivity in spring time among birds

questions.solution:
__
 
• **Hibernation is defined as a state of reduced metabolic activity during winter season among some animals__**.
 
• Many organisms are hibernators such as Fishes, Amphibians and Reptiles.
 
• Snakes, Frogs and Lizards hibernate in cold weather because they are cold blooded animals.
 
• The Hibernators relies on a combination of reserve body fat, stored food supplies etc.
 
• Some animals become dormant in the summer season which is called **__Aestivation__**.
